ios.desc:
Scan a QR. Score a freebie.
Birthday treats, retail samples, café extras — claim codes count down until they’re TAKEN.
Every QR is hiding something free. Qrblox is the key.

WHAT YOU CAN DO
• Scan any QR — camera, screenshot, or photo from your library
• Browse freebies near you and online: birthday party favors, retail samples, café extras, creator drops
• Open a claim page and see how many are left before you tap Claim
• Peek before you open — preview the destination and skip sketchy links
• List a freebie and mint a claim pack with a pink-framed QR ready to print or share
• Generate round or square QR codes for stickers, packaging, and event tables

HOW CLAIMS WORK
Someone lists a freebie (a café, a retailer, a birthday host, a creator). Qrblox unlocks the claim page at qrb.dev/f/{CODE}. Anyone who scans sees what’s left. When it’s gone, the page shows TAKEN. Claim pages open in any browser — no app install needed to view the gift. No payment info, ever.

Qrblox does not give the freebies. The lister does. Qrblox is the key that opens the claim.

SAFETY & LEGITIMACY
• Link preview before you open
• Remaining count → TAKEN so you know when a freebie is gone
• Modest, real freebies — samples, stickers, treats — not luxury prize bait
• You choose what to claim; nothing is charged through the app

Download Qrblox. Scan a QR. Score a freebie — before it’s TAKEN.

quotes.text:
Qrblox is an app that reads the website behind the QR code and chats with you. QR codes could do more to connect businesses and users so I have a history view, notifications, and feeds to send updates. I'd like to add call backs and voice AI for small businesses.

Roast my app? There are dozens of QR code apps, do you just use the native camera or use a QR code app currently? Storing local codes for privacy makes sense, but when you want to stay connected I thought a cloud-based app would be helpful.

Just launched on the Apple app store: https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6737632062?pt=127275939&ct=Show%20HN%207225&mt=8
